disorder-name.detail: 92 pathogenic CNVs and their reciprocal CNVs (duplications and deletions). The study highlights 1q21.1 distal deletion/duplication as primary examples; supplementary results include 15q11.2, 16p11.2, and 16p13.11 deletions/duplications.
disorder-name.supporting_text: "We focused on 92 CNVs proposed to be pathogenic (henceforth 'pathogenic') and their reciprocal CNVs, including both duplications and deletions."

dataset-of-origin.detail: All pathogenic CNV carriers were identified from the UK Biobank cohort (application number 23668).
dataset-of-origin.supporting_text: "we applied these models to understand the neurobiological profile of CNV carriers in the UK Biobank cohort"; "For the genetic CNV data, we focused on the 92 CNVs proposed to be pathogenic, which can be requested from https://biobank.ndph.ox.ac.uk/ukb/app.cgi?id=14421"
dataset-of-origin.location: Fraza2023.pdf.md: Abstract, L19; Methods / Participant demographics and data sources, L341

age.detail: Two analyses reported with model-specific values (IDP model; Jacobian model): IDP analysis (UKB-IDP-CNV, N=263, mean=62.97, sd=8.70) and Jacobian analysis (UKB-CNV, N=375, mean=63.58, sd=7.48). Both share the same age range 46–80 years.

sex.detail: Two analyses reported with model-specific values (IDP model; Jacobian model): IDP analysis (UKB-IDP-CNV, N=263, F 54.4%/M 45.6%) and Jacobian analysis (UKB-CNV, N=375, F 55.4%/M 44.5%). N counts estimated from total N and reported percentages. Table 2 UKB-CNV percentages sum to 99.9% due to rounding in the original paper.
